purpose.question:
The Millard kinetic-metabolism arc, end-to-end. Can the Millard 2017
kinetic central-carbon ODE replace v2ecoli's constraint-based central-
carbon FBA as a drop-in cell engine under the cell-side interface
contract?

Three linked questions:
  1. BUILD     — does the swapped composite (baseline_millard) build and
                 run, with non-trivial live central fluxes (kinetic ODE
                 active, not FBA)?
  2. VALIDATE  — does the Millard whole-cell model recover growth
                 comparable to the FBA baseline, and (once the Millard
                 cell exposes mass-exchange accounting) close mass
                 conservation?
  3. COMPARE   — coupled to the same BiRD reactor and run against the
                 Beulig WT batch prefix, does the Millard kinetic central
                 metabolism track the bioreactor (growth, substrate, gas
                 transfer) BETTER than v2ecoli's WCM-FBA — and how do both
                 compare to the iML1515 genome-scale FBA (Palsson)?
                 Rendered as a structured 3-arm report-card comparison
                 (per-group axis verdicts + categorized divergences),
                 NOT a tolerance gate (execute-and-report, per
                 chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §10).

implementation_requirements.title: Millard cell exposes O2/CO2 exchange to the reactor coupler
implementation_requirements.description:
The Millard cell (baseline_millard) replaced FBA metabolism, so it does NOT
populate `agents.*.environment.exchange` with O2/CO2 — which is what
ReactorCellCoupler reads to drive reactor consumption. Without this the
Millard-coupled reactor is degenerate (cell consumes no reactor O2; DO stays
at saturation). The Millard 2017 model HAS an O2 species + central fluxes, so
translate Millard's O2 uptake / CO2 evolution (central_fluxes) into the cell-
side exchange the coupler consumes (counts into environment.exchange, or a
Millard-aware coupler input). This is the deferred Millard mass-exchange
accounting (also unblocks the wcm-mass-conservation gate on the Millard cell).
unblocks: the Millard arm + wcm-mass-conservation-closes-millard on baseline_millard

implementation_requirements.title: reactor_bird_coupled (Millard variant)
implementation_requirements.description:
A composite coupling baseline_millard (instead of baseline_population's FBA
cell) to BiRDTransportHours + ReactorCellCoupler — i.e. the mbp-03 wiring with
the Millard cell engine swapped in (the cell-side interface contract makes this
a drop-in). Likely a `cell_engine` param on reactor_bird_coupled, or a sibling
reactor_bird_coupled_millard.

implementation_requirements.title: Reuse the mbp-05 Beulig comparison harness for all arms
implementation_requirements.description:
Run the arms against the Beulig batch prefix through the mbp-05 comparison
harness, producing a report_card_verdict.json per arm at the card paths below,
so the report_card_axis tests grade them. Reuses mbp-05's comparison_overlays
+ grader (req: mbp-05 built). Now covers THREE arms — the Millard kinetic cell
(millard_vs_beulig), the WCM-FBA cell (vs_beulig), and the iML1515 genome-scale
FBA contrast (iml1515_vs_beulig).
implementation_requirements.status: done (smoke run; full ~33h batch run is follow-up)

open_questions.text:
pbg-bioreactordesign#2 — dissolved-O2 saturation has the wrong temperature
sign (masked at 298 K; biases c*(O2) high at the 310 K target). All arms
compare against the same biased c*, so the head-to-head is unaffected, but
absolute DO magnitudes vs Beulig are biased until fixed upstream.

The Millard cell accounts nutrient mass via bulk deltas (Millard writes bulk
directly), so the standard MassConservationDeriver (which reads
environment.exchange) historically emitted None on the Millard arm. req-1
routed Millard's uptake/evolution into the cell-side exchange so the
wcm-mass-conservation-closes-millard gate can evaluate. UPDATE (#225 item-5,
2026-06-15): the dominant residual was un-tracked CO2 (decarboxylation) and
H2O (respiration) efflux — the Millard SBML holds HCO3/H2O as FIXED buffers,
so O2/glucose uptake looked like phantom mass import. CO2+H2O efflux is now
reconstructed from reaction stoichiometry and emitted to environment.exchange
(BYPRODUCT_EFFLUX_REACTIONS). The gate now CLOSES on a sustained 100-step
run: conservation_relative_cumulative 8.09 BEFORE -> 0.0284 AFTER (< 0.05),
a ~285x reduction (net mass-in +2.46->+0.09 fg). At 40 ticks it's still ~1.4
during the early flat-growth transient (tiny Δcell_mass denominator) but
converges below 5% by ~80-100 steps. Mass closure is now decoupled from the
slow-growth limitation (see mbp-06 millard-growth-too-slow-to-divide): the
cell still grows far slower than FBA and will not divide, but the boundary
mass balance itself is closed.

visualizations.name: 01_metabolism_swap_growth

config.title: Metabolism swap — cell_mass under the Millard kinetic ODE

visualizations.render:
baseline_millard, 60 steps (1 s/step): cell_mass trajectory with central-
carbon metabolism running as the Millard kinetic ODE (not FBA). Mass is FLAT
at this length (1268.7->1268.8 fg, +0.002%) — growth is not resolvable over
60 s (cell cycle ~2700 s); the figure shows the WCM runs stably under the swap.

visualizations.name: 02_central_fluxes
visualizations.render:
baseline_millard, 60 steps: four key Millard central fluxes (PTS_4 glucose
uptake, CYTBO O2 respiration, PGI glycolysis, PYK pyruvate kinase). Fluxes are
live and non-trivial (PTS_4 ramps 0.070->0.229; PGI dips then recovers),
confirming the kinetic ODE is active.

visualizations.name: 03_env_responsiveness
visualizations.render:
Step-level glucose sweep via MillardPDMPMetabolism.update(external_concentrations
={"GLCx": <mM>}): glucose-uptake flux |PTS_4| vs external glucose, 0.05->20 mM.
Textbook saturation (0.389->0.822 mM/s) — the kinetics respond to the environment.

visualizations.name: 04_reactor_o2_consumption
visualizations.render:
reactor_bird_coupled_millard, 60 steps (cells_per_agent=1e11, gas_flow 2 L/min):
reactor.dissolved_o2 vs o2_saturation (left) and agent O2 exchange counts/step
(right). The Millard cell consumes reactor O2 end-to-end — DO drops 10.2->6.4
mg/L below the ~10.2 mg/L saturation while O2 exchange stays negative (uptake).
